log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Provide a compact reference for identifying countries and territories and their current ISO 3166-1 codes, subdivision-code links and independence status.","tasks":["Look up a country or territory by English name and read across to its codes and status.","Find or compare alpha-2, alpha-3 and numeric codes down their respective columns.","Follow a subdivision-code link for a selected entry.","Read the alphabetical list sequentially while keeping each entry's attributes associated with its name."],"relations":["Each row binds one name to its two letter codes, numeric code, subdivision-code link and independence status.","The alpha-2, alpha-3 and numeric columns are parallel identifiers for the same entry; the subdivision link and independence status provide related information."],"roles":["The header labels six distinct fields; its longer labels may use multiple lines.","The first column identifies entries and anchors row-by-row lookup.","The three code columns support scanning and comparison; the last two columns provide a link and a status."],"keep_whole":["Individual words in names and headers.","Alpha-2, alpha-3 and three-digit numeric codes, including leading zeros.","Subdivision-code link labels and the Independent header."],"may_wrap":["Multiword country and territory names at word spaces.","Multiword headers at natural spaces."],"same_scale":["The alpha-2 and alpha-3 columns should have equal or closely related widths because they serve parallel tasks.","The three code columns should read as a compact group; names and subdivision links warrant more space because their content is longer."],"h_vs_v":"The viewport cannot accommodate every header and value on one line. Wrapping selected headers costs height once, while wrapping names can increase individual row heights throughout the table; preserving complete subdivision links and compact codes makes cross-row scanning more reliable."},"designs":[{"widths":[190,88,88,86,155,112],"strategy":"Give names generous space while keeping the three code columns compact and subdivision links on one line."},{"widths":[160,96,96,100,155,112],"strategy":"Give the code group more room for its headers and comparisons, accepting more wrapping in longer names."},{"widths":[220,74,74,84,155,112],"strategy":"Prioritize continuous reading of names by narrowing the parallel code columns and allowing their headers to wrap."}]}
